artboards.title: A block is what you place

annotations.text: The archetype is papercut's, not the project's — a fixed set to start, extensible later. What the artist meets is the block and the material.

CORRECTED: an earlier draft of the Shapes board drew 3x3 neighbourhoods and drifted into blob thinking. Authoring stays on the corner model — 16 arrangements a pairing, 15 drawn. Inside and outside corners are already among them.

THE FORK. Mitring costs no art and breaks on a texture with a direction. Drawing the seam costs two pieces per wall material AND a second kind of tag — one chosen by what the geometry does rather than by the four materials at a corner.

Proposed: both. A slot left empty is mitred, so the second tag kind exists in the model but is optional in every sheet.

Corner tags are filled by pointing at ONE tile — the block reads the other fourteen. Named slots are filled one at a time. A ground material has no named slots, so the simple case shows a single block and nothing else.
Layers, Authoring and Format predate the block, the archetype and the corner correction. Kept for the GID scheme and the block geometry; to be redrawn once the model settles.
